literature.title: Long-Term Control of HIV by CCR5 Delta32/Delta32 Stem-Cell Transplantation
literature.authors: Hütter G, Nowak D, Mossner M, Ganepola S, Müßig A, Allers K, Schneider T, Hofmann J, Kücherer C, Blau O, Blau IW, Hofmann WK, Thiel E
literature.evidence_level: Clinical Landmark (Case Report - The Berlin Patient)
literature.summary: First clinical proof of concept: Allogeneic stem cell transplantation from a homozygous CCR5-Δ32 donor achieved complete, sustained HIV-1 remission without antiretroviral therapy for over 12 years.
literature.uncertainty: Allogeneic HSCT with myeloablative conditioning carries ~20-30% mortality risk; not viable as a general cure for non-malignant HIV patients. Highlights need for targeted autologous ex-vivo editing.

literature.title: HIV-1 remission following CCR5Δ32/Δ32 haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation
literature.authors: Gupta RK, Abdul-jawad S, McCoy LE, Mok HP, Peppa D, Salgado M, Martinez-Picado J, Nijhuis M, Wensing AMJ, Lee H, et al.
literature.evidence_level: Clinical Landmark (Case Report - The London Patient)
literature.summary: Second documented case of sustained HIV-1 remission (The London Patient, Adam Castillejo) after reduced-intensity chemotherapy and CCR5-Δ32 donor HSCT, proving Berlin patient was not an anomaly.
literature.uncertainty: Confirms CCR5 as the primary therapeutic gate; also revealed risk of viral rebound if CXCR4-tropic viral quasispecies are present (co-receptor tropism switch).

literature.title: CRISPR-Edited Stem Cells in a Patient with HIV and Acute Lymphocytic Leukemia
literature.authors: Xu L, Wang J, Liu Y, Xie L, Su B, Mou D, Wang L, He T, Wang X, Zhang F, et al.
literature.summary: CRISPR-Cas9 was used to ablate CCR5 in CD34+ HSPCs followed by transplantation in a patient with HIV-1 and acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Edit was stable for >19 months without detectable off-target cuts.
literature.uncertainty: CCR5 editing efficiency in engrafted peripheral cells was only 5-8%, insufficient to completely eliminate viral load upon antiretroviral interruption. Proves safety but underscores need for higher on-target editing efficiency.

literature.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Gene Editing for Sickle Cell Disease and beta-Thalassemia
literature.authors: Frangoul H, Altshuler D, Cappellini MD, Chen YS, Domm J, Eustace BK, Foell J, de la Fuente J, Grupp S, Handgretinger R, et al.
literature.summary: Targeted disruption of the erythroid-specific enhancer of BCL11A via Cas9 electroporation restored high-level fetal hemoglobin expression, eliminating vaso-occlusive crises in SCD and transfusion dependency in beta-thalassemia.
literature.uncertainty: Off-target cutting monitored via GUIDE-seq and deep sequencing showed no genotoxic translocation; long-term durability of clonal hematopoiesis requires multi-year surveillance.

literature.title: Optimized sgRNA design to maximize activity and minimize off-target effects of CRISPR-Cas9
literature.authors: Doench JG, Fusi N, Sullender M, Hegde M, Vaimberg EW, Donovan KF, Smith I, Tothova Z, Wilen C, Orchard R, et al.
literature.summary: Developed predictive machine learning model (Rule Set 2) incorporating position-specific nucleotide preferences, GC content, and melting temperatures to score Cas9 on-target cleavage efficiency.
literature.uncertainty: Trained predominantly on standard human reference sequences in cell lines. Local SNPs in primary patient genomes can shift cleavage scores and invalidate generic predictions.
